4. // PhysicalAddress — Specifications
5. //
6. // A `PhysicalAddress` abstracts to a single mathematical integer: the raw
7. // physical address (`PhysicalAddress@ : int`, defined by the `View` impl in
8. // `phys.rs`, delegating to the inner `VirtualAddress`). The only derived notion
9. // callers reason about is the *frame* the address lies in
10. // (`addr / FRAME_SIZE == addr >> FRAME_SHIFT`), used to index the frame
11. // allocator's bitmaps / refcount arrays.
12. //
13. // Trust-boundary helpers pin the not-yet-verified `arch` `FrameNumber` type and
14. // the `arch`/`sys` library-edge constants/methods this module calls. They mirror
15. // the existing `sys`/`arch` `assume_specification` boundaries the codebase
16. // already draws (`::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` in `frame.rs`, the `Address` trait
17. // methods in `page.spec.rs` / `kframe.spec.rs`). `spec_page_size()` is the
18. // canonical frame size, re-exported from `crate::hal::mem` (defined alongside
19. // `FrameAddress`); `FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE == spec_page_size()`.
20. 
21. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
22. verus! {
23. 
24. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
25. 
26. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
27. // `View`/datatype registration reachable here. Declare it to Verus as an opaque
28. // external datatype so it may appear in spec-fn parameters and the
29. // `assume_specification`s below. Its internals are not modeled (`external_body`):
30. // its abstract index is projected by `spec_frame_raw_value`.
31. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
32. #[verifier::external_body]
33. pub struct ExFrameNumber(FrameNumber);
34. 
35. // ── Frame-number trust-boundary projections (arch `FrameNumber`) ──────────────
36. //
37. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
38. // `View` impl reachable here (orphan rule). Its abstract index is therefore
39. // projected by an uninterpreted ghost function, exactly as `view_design.md`
40. // prescribes. `spec_max_frame_number()` denotes `FrameNumber::MAX`.
41. 
42. // The integer index of a frame number (`0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`).
43. pub uninterp spec fn spec_frame_raw_value(frame: FrameNumber) -> int;
44. 
45. // The largest representable frame number (`arch FrameNumber::MAX`).
46. pub uninterp spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int;
47. 
48. // ── Derived spec helpers over the View domain (`int`) ─────────────────────────
49. 
50. // The frame an address lies in: exact integer division, independent of whether
51. // the implementation shifts (`>> FRAME_SHIFT`) or divides (`/ FRAME_SIZE`).
52. pub open spec fn spec_frame_number(addr_view: int) -> int {
53.     addr_view / spec_page_size()
54. }
55. 
56. // The base (frame-aligned) address of a frame index: `frame * FRAME_SIZE`.
57. pub open spec fn spec_from_number(frame_view: int) -> int {
58.     frame_view * spec_page_size()
59. }
60. 
61. // ── `arch`/`sys` library-edge `assume_specification`s ─────────────────────────
62. 
63. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE` is the frame size (alias of `PAGE_SIZE`), tied to the
64. // canonical `spec_page_size()`.
65. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE ] -> (result: usize)
66.     ensures
67.         result == spec_page_size(),
68. ;
69. 
70. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT == log2(FRAME_SIZE)`. Bounded below the pointer width
71. // so `raw_addr >> FRAME_SHIFT` is well-defined.
72. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT ] -> (result: usize)
73.     ensures
74.         result < usize::BITS,
75. ;
76. 
77. // `VirtualAddress::new` is a pure newtype constructor: the wrapped value is the
78. // abstract address. (`sys` library edge; the inner module is not yet verified.)
79. pub assume_specification[ VirtualAddress::new ](value: usize) -> (result: VirtualAddress)
80.     ensures
81.         result@ == value as int,
82. ;
83. 
84. // `<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value` is pure newtype identity: the
85. // returned raw `usize` equals the abstract address.
86. pub assume_specification[ <VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value ](
87.     addr: VirtualAddress,
88. ) -> (result: usize)
89.     ensures
90.         result as int == addr@,
91. ;
92. 
93. // `FrameNumber::into_raw_value` projects a frame number to its index; every
94. // `FrameNumber` value is in range (`0 ..= MAX`) by construction.
95. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::into_raw_value ](frame: FrameNumber) -> (result: usize)
96.     ensures
97.         result as int == spec_frame_raw_value(frame),
98.         0 <= spec_frame_raw_value(frame) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
99. ;
100. 
101. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value` succeeds iff `value <= MAX`, preserving the index.
102. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::from_raw_value ](value: usize) -> (result: Option<FrameNumber>)
103.     ensures
104.         match result {
105.             Some(f) => value as int <= spec_max_frame_number()
106.                 && spec_frame_raw_value(f) == value as int,
107.             None => value as int > spec_max_frame_number(),
108.         },
109. ;
110. 
111. // ── Type invariant ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
112. //
113. // Every `PhysicalAddress` a verified constructor produces has a *representable
114. // frame number*: `self@ / FRAME_SIZE <= FrameNumber::MAX`. This is the load-
115. // bearing fact that makes `into_frame_number` total (its internal
116. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never panics), which the frame
117. // allocator relies on when using the result directly as a bitmap / refcount
118. // index. It is *not* alignment (MMIO addresses may be unaligned) and *not*
119. // RAM-validity (`from_mmio_address` deliberately bypasses that check).
120. impl PhysicalAddress {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
123.     }
